intro.title: Build tabs with keyboard navigation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an accessible tabbed interface that users can navigate using their keyboard. You will learn how to manage component state to track the active tab and handle user interactions. The core programming concepts involve using React hooks like useState for state management and useEffect for side effects, along with event handlers for keyboard inputs. You'll work with JSX to structure the tab buttons and content panels, ensuring proper ARIA attributes for accessibility. By the end, you'll have a functional tab component that responds to arrow keys and the Enter or Space key for activation.
intro.usecase: Tabbed interfaces with keyboard navigation are essential for accessibility and productivity in modern web applications. You'll find them in content-heavy dashboards like analytics platforms (Google Analytics, Mixpanel) where users switch between different data views, or in admin panels where sections like Users, Settings, and Reports are organized in tabs. Developers implement this pattern in documentation sites with code examples, e-commerce product detail pages with Description/Reviews/Specs tabs, and any multi-panel UI where keyboard users need efficient navigation without reaching for their mouse.
